types.description: The primary key — one per entity; @fields names its column(s), @generation the value strategy.
types.whenToUse: Every entity needs exactly one — names the primary-key field(s) and how the value is generated. Always declare it.

children.name: fields
children.description: The field name(s) composing this identity. Single-element for a simple PK/index, multiple for a composite.

types.description: A secondary unique index on one or more fields. Always enforces uniqueness — use index.lookup for non-unique query-performance indexes.
types.whenToUse: A column or set of columns must be unique (e.g. email, slug, composite business key). For a plain non-unique index, use index.lookup instead.

children.name: fields
children.description: The field name(s) composing this identity. Single-element for a simple unique index, multiple for a composite unique constraint.

types.description: A foreign-key reference to another entity (@references target; @enforce toggles a physical FK).
types.whenToUse: This entity holds a foreign key to another. Declare it to generate the FK constraint + typed navigation, instead of a loose id field you join on by hand.

children.name: fields
children.description: The field name(s) composing this identity. Single-element for a simple PK/index, multiple for a composite.

children.name: references
children.description: Target of the reference. Bare entity name (e.g. 'Program') resolves to that entity's primary identity. Dotted forms ('Program.id' or 'Program.fieldA,fieldB') target an explicit field set on the entity.

children.name: enforce
children.description: When true (default), the backend physically enforces the reference (SQL FK constraint, document validation rule, graph edge guarantee). Set false to declare a logical reference for navigation/typing/codegen only — the value may dangle at the backend level.
